name: Typewise
task: A help desk, tickets or a shared inbox
summary: AI agents for customer service that resolve requests end to end and take action in the systems you already run - CRM, ERP, billing, commerce - configured in plain language.
best_for: customer-service teams with real ticket volume that want AI agents to resolve requests end to end and act inside the systems they already run — CRM, ERP, billing, commerce — with approval steps and human handover as they raise the automation level
skip_if: your helpdesk's built-in AI answers already absorb the volume, or your channel mix leans on phone support — their home page lists voice among the channels while their own SMB page still marks it "coming soon", so pin that down before you sign
honest_knock: The bill has two parts and both are published: a base fee from $99 and a resolution rate from $2 (pay as you go) down to $1 with volume packages. The meter is published too — a ticket closed end to end counts as one resolution, a hand-off to a person counts as half, and a ticket passed straight through or flagged is free. So a conversation the AI cannot finish still bills, at half rate, which is fair but worth budgeting for. What the page still does not say is whether a reopened ticket counts again; get that in writing before the trial. The ROI calculator on their site is the vendor's own arithmetic; the pilot is where you replace it with yours.

pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-09-23 and again, unchanged, 2026-09-27 on typewise.app/pricing) A base plan plus a per-resolution rate. Starter is $99 a month or $999 a year with 1 user, email and chat, a $20 monthly AI Operator budget and pay-as-you-go resolutions at $2 each. Growth is $599 a month or $5,999 a year with 5 users, all digital channels, a $100 AI Operator budget and volume packages that bring resolutions down to $1. Business is $2,000 a month billed annually with 5 users, 3 workspaces (multi-brand), a $500 AI Operator budget, two custom integration days a year and a success consultant. Enterprise is quoted and adds SSO, a custom DPA, unlimited workspaces, a $1,500 AI Operator budget and five integration days. Additional users are $89 a month on every plan - an add-on, not a starting price. Every plan starts with a 14-day trial of 100 resolution credits and $10 of AI Operator credit, no card. The page defines the meter: a full resolution counts once, a hand-off to a person counts as half, and unresolved or flagged tickets are free. Prices are in USD and shown in EUR, GBP or CHF at parity depending on your location. Correction 23 Sep 2026: our 5 Sep reading put unlimited workspaces and the $1,500 budget on Business; on the current page those belong to Enterprise. History: in August 2026 the only published number was 'starting from $1 per resolution' on the home page and /pricing returned a 404.

compare_with.name: Intercom Fin or your helpdesk's native AI
compare_with.why: the honest comparison is where the work happens: Fin lives inside Intercom's own desk, while Typewise sells itself as a layer above the stack you already run, reading and writing in CRM, ERP and commerce systems. Already on Intercom? The native option starts ahead. Support work spread across several systems? That layer is the argument — ask both what counts as a resolution before you compare the price

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 during the trial, without a card, without connecting a channel and without publishing anything: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser, using only the Simulator. We gave the AI a two-line return policy as a text knowledge source, asked four customer questions with known right answers, changed the return window from 14 to 30 days, asked again, and exported the tickets.
findings: Once the knowledge source was ready, the answers matched it: an unopened vase after 5 days got 'yes, you can return it' citing the 14-day policy for unopened items, and an opened lamp got 'not eligible for return or refund'. Asked about shipping to Norway, which the source did not cover, it said it couldn't find a verified answer and handed the conversation to a human ('Needs agent takeover'). It did not make anything up.

Changing the rule from 14 to 30 days took effect in the Simulator straight away: an unopened candle holder after 20 days first got 'no ... outside our return window' and, after the change, 'yes ... within 30 days of delivery for a full refund'. The source showed 'Not published yet', so this was the unpublished version.

Our very first question, asked while the knowledge source still said 'Analyzing' (it turned 'Ready' after about a minute), was handed over to a human in full. Asked again once the source was ready, it was answered.

Plan & limits showed 'Trial · 92 days remaining' on the day of sign-up, against 14 days in Typewise's documentation, with no payment method, 1,000 resolutions, 50K Nova (AI Operator) credits and one agent seat. Simulator conversations did not count as resolutions (still 0 of 1,000).

Every Simulator conversation became a ticket with an automatic title, priority and status. 'Export all' downloads an Excel file straight away with 16 columns per ticket, including the AI summary, status, language and CSAT, but not the conversation messages themselves.

Knowledge sources can be a live URL, web search, a website import, a file (PDF, Word or Excel only), text, or 'Ask a team member'. Parts of the interface showed Dutch text next to English, and once text we typed into the description landed in the name field.

came_along: One row per ticket (6 rows, 16 columns): ticket ID, title, AI summary, customer name and email, channel, priority, status, assignee, team, resolution status, language, CSAT score and comment, created and last activity

exit_test.note: A check of this export route with synthetic records, on the account and date stated. Re-importing the export was not tested. Friction is described, not scored; this is not a verdict on the product.
